day_summary: PREMARKET GAP FADED — REGIME NOT CLEARED; AAPL/MSFT PRICE INCREASES DRAGGED MAG7. NVDA gapped to ~$207 premarket on the Micron $50B Q4 guide + Qualcomm Dragonfly dual-catalyst, then faded as PCE printed core 3.4% (1 bp above 3.3% consensus, not the cold print needed to clear regime gates). The defining session development: Apple announced price increases on iPhone, iPad, and Mac citing higher memory costs; Microsoft raised Xbox prices on the same rationale. Both stocks sold off hard (AAPL −6.5% to ~$274; MSFT −5.1% to $354.32) and dragged the entire Mag7 complex lower. NVDA closed ~$196.87 (−1.99% from $200.81 prev close). MU closed $1,165.94 (+~17%) — the direct memory demand beneficiary of the AAPL/MSFT price-increase signal. SPX finished 7,357.49 (−0.01%). Regime remains fully breached: SPX 7,357 < 7,460 gate, VIX 18.63 > 17 gate, DXY 101.43 > 100 gate. The AI demand thesis is CONFIRMED (OEMs raising consumer prices rather than canceling memory orders), but the regime framework requires all three gates to clear before sizing. Decision: HOLD — do not add or exit.

analysis:
## Technical analysis

**Session outcome:** NVDA gapped to ~$208 at the open on dual-catalyst optimism (Micron + Qualcomm), then faded all day as PCE printed 1 bp above consensus and AAPL/MSFT announced consumer hardware price increases. Closed ~$196.87 (−1.96%), below the June 24 close of $200.81.

**Regime status:** All three gates remain breached: SPX 7,357.49 < 7,460, VIX 18.63 > 17, DXY 101.43 > 100. Three consecutive closes below 7,460 have converted that level to resistance.

**Demand thesis confirmed:** AAPL/MSFT raising consumer hardware prices citing memory costs is the strongest possible real-world validation of AI HBM demand. The sell-off was not fundamental — it was multiple compression on Mag7 brand risk (demand elasticity unknown) and macro-regime friction (PCE core 3.4%).

**Decision:** HOLD at medium conviction. Stop $195 two-close basis. Add only on SPX > 7,460 AND VIX < 17 simultaneously.
